Brett Lindstrom

America First candidate for Governor and Lt. Governor, Nebraska · Challenger

Former Nebraska state senator

Brett Lindstrom of Omaha represented District 18 in the Nebraska Legislature from 2015 to 2023 and finished third in the 2022 Republican primary for governor. In 2026 he tried to qualify as a nonpartisan candidate for governor with running mate Mike Picard, but he fell short after the Secretary of State found many petition signatures invalid, many of them flagged as fraudulent. On Sept. 1, 2026, after the Nebraska Supreme Court cleared the new America First Party's recognition, he filed as the party's nominee for governor.

Where Lindstrom stands

Property taxes
Proposes moving major property classes toward rolling valuation averaging to reduce swings in valuations. Proposes lowering schools' maximum operating levy from $1.05 to 50 cents per $100 of valuation over time, with more state aid as finances allow.
Economy and agriculture
Proposes valuing farmland mostly on productive income (about 80% income, 20% market value) instead of 75% of market value. Supports keeping more of Nebraska's farm products processed in-state.
Government spending
Says the current administration spent through a historic cash reserve, raided cash funds and made billions in commitments without a sustainable way to pay for them. Argues 'you cannot cut your way to prosperity, and you cannot spend your way to growth.'
Data centers
Proposes that the state talk less about data centers by name and more about digital infrastructure, secure cloud services, computing capacity and cybersecurity. Supports protecting public power and expanding the electric grid ahead of demand.
Affordability and housing
Proposes building housing near existing jobs and infrastructure, recruiting former Nebraskans back to the state, and investing in regional growth hubs.
Economy and public schools
Supports coordinating K-12 schools, community colleges, apprenticeships and employers as one workforce pipeline. Supports finishing rural broadband deployment.
Bipartisanship
Says neither major party is willing to tell Nebraskans the truth. Says he is not running a protest or 'spoiler' campaign.
